newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses but end off on jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses but end off on jitters.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared earlier losses but still closed sharply lower Monday after zigzagging on fears of primary rate hikes and a volatile peso.

"We were a little surprised by the market's performance... Basically the (downward) movement was due to a volatile exchange rate and forecasts of increased (primary) rates tomorrow," said Alfredo Diaz, an equity analyst with the Inverlat brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended down 45.06 points, or 1.17 percent, at 3,795.92.
Trading volume was subdued at 57.5 million shares.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts plunged 10.4 centavos at the open to 8.05 per dollar, but partially recovered to close at 7.9950 per dollar.
Overnight rates on Cetes, or Treasury bills, meanwhile closed at 22 percent, substantially above secondary rates at the beginning of last week.
Traders said higher secondary interest rates and a weaker peso set the stage for gains of up to 3 percentage points in bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at Tuesday's primary auction.

Analysts said the U.S. government's process of certifying Mexico as an ally in the war on drugs also weighed down share prices in Mexico. Congressional ratification was still needed for the administration's decision to certifify Mexico Friday.
On the broad market, 99 stocks changed hands, of which decliners outnumbered gainers by 70 to 16.
A notable decliner was cement company Cemex, whose B shares fell 50 centavos (6 cents) to 34.00 pesos ($4.25)

Another heavily traded decliner was corn flour and tortilla maker Maseca, which ended off 50 centavos (6 cents) at 9.08 pesos ($1.14). Traders said the stock may have fallen due to a forthcoming IPO by competitors Minsa.
Shares listed by Maseca's holding company Gruma also fell, ending off two pesos (25 cents) at 37.00 pesos ($4.63).
Soft-drinks bottler Gemex headed the decliners' list, down 84 centavos (11 cents) to 12.80 pesos ($1.60) on profit-taking, traders said.
Financial group Serfin headed the gainers, up 30 centavos (4 cents) to 3.50 pesos (44 cents) on speculative buying after the market hit the stock hard last week, traders said.
